To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The attitudes of primary care physicians (PCPs) toward cancer-prevention clinical trials (CPCT) vary according to their perception of the trial's relevance to their practice and their perception of the potential risks and benefits to patients and physicians.

(1) the majority of physicians in our study were willing to participate in a clinical trial, (2) physicians who were not willing to participate were more concerned about the potential risks of participation, (3) physicians who were willing to participate were less concerned about the risks of participation, and (4) physicians were more likely to participate if the clinical trial was for a condition that is not life-threatening.
